artifacts.summary: Best practices for structuring large markdown literature files with index.json metadata: chapter-level splitting into subdirectories, JSON master index mirroring .claude/context/index.json schema, keyword-overlap retrieval mirroring memory-retrieve.sh, token-budget-aware greedy selection

memory_candidates.content: The specs/literature/ directory holds markdown exports of academic books/papers for --lit injection. Best practice: split book-length files (>50KB) into chapter-level .md files in subdirectories (specs/literature/{bibkey}/), with a master index.json at specs/literature/index.json using the same schema as .claude/context/index.json. Paper-length files (<50KB, e.g. bentzen_2023.md) stay as single files. The retrieval script scores entries by keyword overlap against the task description and focus_prompt, then greedily selects within a 4000-token budget — identical architecture to memory-retrieve.sh.

Current specs/literature/*.md files lack semantic markdown headers. blackburn_2001.md uses <!-- Page N --> comments (66 pages), mendelson_2016.md uses ## Page N headers (492 pages), hughes_1996.md has no headers at all, chagrov_1997.md has OCR artifact # lines (not real headings). Manual chapter extraction guided by each book's table of contents is required — automatic header-based splitting produces meaningless page-granular chunks.
